content.text:
I didn't change anything in `orders`. I hit the tool-call limit before I could run the update, and while checking the data I found a problem with updating by customer.

**What I found:**
- `orders_staging` has 40 rows covering 35 customers, and every row has its own order `id`.
- The customers in staging have 110 orders in `orders`. Only 15 of those orders also appear in staging by `id`, and for those 15 the `customer_id` matches. Eight of the 15 have a different status in staging.
- **Matching on customer alone doesn't give one answer.** Customers 2, 9, 16, 48 and 55 each have two staging rows with different statuses, so there's no single status to give all their orders. Matching on customer would also overwrite about 95 orders that staging doesn't list at all.
- 25 staging rows have no matching order in `orders`. These look like new orders, not status changes.

**What I suggest:** update by order `id`, which changes only the 15 matching orders (8 of them will actually get a new status):

```sql
MERGE INTO orders o
USING orders_staging s
ON o.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET status = s.status;
```

This leaves the 25 unmatched staging rows out. If you want them added as new orders, a `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT` clause would do it.

Do you want me to run it this way? If you really meant every order for those customers, tell me which status the five customers with two different staging statuses should get.
